To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) RDF view selection is a challenging problem that can be solved by adapting the existing relational techniques, and that (ii) the use of implicit triples in query reformulation and view selection significantly reduces the number of views that have to be selected.

(1) the view selection algorithms that we propose are able to handle large RDF datasets, and (2) the use of implicit data in the selection process leads to a significant reduction in the number of views needed to be materialized.

(1) view selection in the context of the Semantic Web is a problem that is significantly different from its relational counterpart, and requires novel algorithms; (2) view selection algorithms for the Semantic Web are able to scale to large RDF data sets and to handle large numbers of queries and views; (3) our algorithms are able to select view sets that are both efficient and effective in the context of RDF data, as demonstrated by a number of experiments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of view selection in Semantic Web databases.
the problem of selecting views to be materialised in a Semantic Web database so as to improve query processing performance.
the problem of selecting the best set of views in order to optimize a query workload for a Semantic Web database.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach is a good solution to the problem of selecting views for Semantic Web Databases.
our techniques are very promising for the Semantic Web context, and that they scale significantly better than the state-of-the-art relational ones.
the proposed techniques are effective in selecting a set of materialized views that significantly reduce the query processing costs in a Semantic Web database.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Semantic Web is a challenging environment for query optimization and database design, which requires a careful consideration of the trade-off between query processing, view maintenance and storage costs.
we have developed a set of techniques to select a set of views in the context of Semantic Web databases that scale to very large datasets and are able to handle the implicit triples in the data.
we have developed an efficient view selection algorithm for Semantic Web databases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the view materialization problem is not a mere adaptation of the relational one, but requires novel algorithms and techniques.
, in the context of Semantic Web databases, it is important to take into account both the explicit and implicit parts of the data, as well as to exploit the specific properties of the RDF data model.
, in a Semantic Web database context, the view selection problem is much harder than the relational one and that, in spite of this, our methods are able to find good view sets in reasonable time.
